EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Mom's First Car Spent 30 Years in the Garage, Now She Wants To See Her Son Driving It
15 photos
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube
This 42-year-old Volkswagen Scirocco spent 30 years locked inside a garage. Its owner got it from her mom, but life happened, and she just stopped driving it at some point. Now, with a son passionate about cars from the 1980s, she wants to pass it on to him. But first, it needs to be cleaned up and fixed.
Juliet remembers that her parents bought the 1984 Volkswagen Scirocco almost new in 1985 after it had served as a demo car at the dealership. Juliet’s mom drove it quite a lot in the 1980s. It meant the world to her. When Juliet turned 16, she passed it on to her daughter.
When Juliet's mom passed away, her father couldn't let the car go. So he parked it, and nobody ever touched it again. Years passed, and Juliet’s first car is still parked in the family garage. It doesn't run, it doesn't drive, and it is covered in a thick layer of dust and grime.
Juliet’s son is now 25, and she would love to give him a chance to drive it. So she called the detailers to wash 30 years of neglect off her first car. But it won't be easy. The car is sitting on four tires that were slashed at some point. Some kids from the neighborhood did it when Juliet’s mother was in hospice.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube RJ of WD Detailing trailers the Scirocco to the studio, and surprisingly, with a bit of starting fluid sprayed into the intake, the engine fires up right away, but it dies right out. A mechanic will take care of that later. Now, the first step is removing the wheels, but RJ needs Miss Persuasion, which is actually a sledgehammer, to help him hammer the wheels off.
Then vacuuming is the next step before the power wash. But as water makes the dirt collected over three decades vanish, it reveals the poor condition of the silver paint. RJ uses a degreaser to lift years of grime off the 42-year-old paint, which has become very vulnerable. Rust has bitten chunks out of the doors and fenders.
The interior tells the exact same story. The one who cleans it up is Mike, who owns a Scirocco himself. His is a 16-valve 1987 unit, looking like it just rolled off the production line. This is what he wants to see in the silver 1984 Scirocco with a blue interior, entirely covered in grime and dust that it has collected over the years.
And it’s not just the grime and dust. Mike is sure that mice have built a home on board the Volkswagen and is determined to find it. While searching for the mice, he found an old Pepsi can and a Tropicana juice bottle from the early 1990s.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube The Compressed air and the vacuum cleaner, the stain extractor, and the steamer won’t work miracles on a carpet that mice had their fair share of fun with. So it needs to come out. Otherwise, the Scirocco would be a rolling biohazard. The detailers scrub every single inch underneath it.
Popping the hood reveals how years have taken their toll on the car. The insulation is disintegrating the moment RJ steers his vacuum cleaner toward it. The engine bay is just as bad. It contains 30 years of oil leaks and fluid spills, which make the detailer label it a disaster zone. He has to clean it up before Aki, the mechanic, arrives at the scene. He is well aware that one wrong move and the car, with all the wires and hoses exposed, might never start again.
At least not with this engine under the hood. The 1984 Volkswagen Scirocco came with a 1.8-liter inline-four with mechanical fuel injection, producing 90 horsepower (91 metric horsepower) and 100 pound-feet (136 Newton meters) of torque for a top speed of 111 mph (178 kph).
RJ lets his citrus degreaser do its job before he rinses it off and prepares the territory for Aki, the 21-year-old mechanic who is half the age of the car, to do more than just make the inline-four run for a few seconds like they did the moment they rolled the car off the trailer into their studio.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube To access the fuel pump and see the condition it is in, he needs to remove the rear seats. It needs to be replaced. Three days later, when the new one arrives, they realize they waited three days only to find out they ordered the wrong pump.
The bad news is that mice even made a nest on top of the fuel injection system. But he can deal with that. He also needed to deal with a rusty fuel tank. Replacing it was not an option, so he came up with a fuel cell in the trunk. Now, $2,000 later, when the inline-four fires up, it doesn’t shut down instantly. It idles and sounds like "your grandpa's tractor," Aki says.
So now, RJ can take it back to Juliet, who is waiting in the company of her son. The young man has never seen the Volkswagen Scirocco running and driving. Juliet can’t believe her ears when she hears the engine.
" You are a miracle worker ," she tells RJ as she applauds his work. A few days before, the car was just a big mouse nest. Now, it looks like it has never even sat parked, untouched for 30 years.
